name: Internal jugular vein
function: Main venous drainage of the brain, face and neck. Begins at the jugular bulb as the continuation of the sigmoid sinus and ends by joining the subclavian vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of sigmoid sinus at jugular foramen (superior bulb); receives inferior petrosal sinus, pharyngeal, common facial, lingual, superior and middle thyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends in the carotid sheath lateral to ICA then CCA, with vagus nerve posterior between them; runs deep to SCM; inferior bulb has a bicuspid valve

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint to form the brachiocephalic vein (venous angle)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical lymph node chain along its length; ansa cervicalis on its anterior surface; accessory nerve crosses it near the posterior belly of digastric

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior bulb (in the jugular fossa, receives the sigmoid sinus); inferior bulb (dilation above the union with the subclavian vein, valve above it)

pearl: Central line: insert at apex of the triangle between the SCM heads, aiming toward the ipsilateral nipple; IJV lies lateral to the carotid. Lemierre syndrome = septic IJV thrombophlebitis (Fusobacterium) after pharyngitis.

name: External jugular vein
function: Superficial vein draining the scalp and face around the ear and the lateral neck; runs on SCM under platysma and empties into the subclavian vein. Less reliable than the IJV for JVP because of its valves.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Union of posterior auricular vein and posterior division of the retromandibular vein near the angle of the mandible, within or just below the parotid

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends obliquely across SCM deep to platysma, pierces the investing fascia in the posterior triangle just above the clavicle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Subclavian vein; receives posterior external jugular, transverse cervical, suprascapular and anterior jugular veins near its termination

details.label: Relations
details.value: Great auricular nerve runs parallel and posterior to it on SCM; transverse cervical nerve passes forward deep to it; covered by platysma

pearl: Visible EJV distension in a seated patient suggests raised venous pressure, but JVP is read from the IJV. A cut EJV where it pierces the deep fascia is held open and can suck air: venous air embolism.

name: Anterior jugular vein and jugular venous arch
function: Paired superficial veins of the anterior neck that drain the submental and infrahyoid skin; the two sides are joined above the manubrium by the jugular venous arch.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Submental and superficial submandibular veins near the hyoid; receives a communicating vein from the facial / common facial vein (or retromandibular vein) in the upper neck

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends near the midline superficial to the infrahyoid strap muscles; turns laterally in the suprasternal space (of Burns) deep to SCM

details.label: Drains into
details.value: External jugular vein (or subclavian) at the root of the neck

details.label: Relations
details.value: Jugular venous arch connects right and left anterior jugulars in the suprasternal space just above the sternal notch

pearl: The jugular venous arch and anterior jugular veins lie in the path of a low tracheostomy or suprasternal incision; identify and ligate them to avoid troublesome bleeding.

name: Posterior external jugular vein
function: Drains the skin and superficial muscles of the occipital scalp and upper back of the neck, running between splenius and trapezius, then joins the external jugular vein just below the middle of its course.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superficial veins of the occipital scalp and posterior neck (communicates with occipital vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Begins in the occipital region, descends in the back of the neck between splenius capitis and trapezius, then emerges onto SCM to join the EJV

details.label: Drains into
details.value: External jugular vein just below the middle of its course (about mid-SCM level), not in the lower third

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to trapezius and superficial to splenius in the upper neck; near the lesser occipital nerve and cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus

pearl: Small tributary that bleeds freely in posterior triangle procedures (lymph node biopsy); of little hemodynamic consequence but easily mistaken for the EJV.

name: Subclavian vein
function: Continuation of the axillary vein draining the upper limb; passes behind the clavicle and joins the IJV to form the brachiocephalic vein. A major central venous access route.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of axillary vein at the outer border of the first rib; receives external jugular vein and, at its union with the IJV, the thoracic duct (left) or right lymphatic duct

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs medially behind the clavicle, anterior to the anterior scalene muscle and phrenic nerve, over the first rib; separated from the subclavian artery by anterior scalene

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins IJV behind the sternoclavicular joint to form the brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pleural apex and subclavian artery lie posterior; valves near its termination

pearl: Infraclavicular line: needle under the clavicle at the junction of its medial and middle thirds, aimed at the sternal notch. Lowest infection rate but highest pneumothorax risk; non-compressible, so avoid in coagulopathy, and avoid in CKD (stenosis would jeopardize a future AV fistula).

name: Brachiocephalic veins
function: Formed by the IJV and subclavian vein on each side; right and left unite to form the SVC. Receive the vertebral, inferior thyroid and internal thoracic veins from the neck.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: IJV + subclavian vein at the venous angle; tributaries: vertebral, inferior thyroid, internal thoracic, first posterior intercostal, (left) superior intercostal

details.label: Course
details.value: Right is short (~2.5 cm) and vertical; left is longer (~6 cm), crosses the midline behind the manubrium and in front of the arch branches to join the right

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior vena cava, behind the first right costal cartilage

details.label: Relations
details.value: Left brachiocephalic vein lies anterior to the brachiocephalic trunk and left common carotid; thymus and manubrium anterior

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Right brachiocephalic vein (short, vertical); left brachiocephalic vein (long, crosses behind the manubrium, receives the inferior thyroid veins)

pearl: The left brachiocephalic vein may lie above the sternal notch in children, placing it at risk during tracheostomy. It is compressed by mediastinal masses in SVC syndrome.

name: Venous angle (jugulo-subclavian junction)
function: Junction of the IJV and subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint, where the brachiocephalic vein begins. The thoracic duct (left) and right lymphatic duct enter here.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: IJV meeting the subclavian vein; receives the thoracic duct on the left and the right lymphatic duct on the right

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies behind the medial end of the clavicle and sternoclavicular joint, anterior to the anterior scalene and phrenic nerve

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Right vagus crosses anterior to the first part of the right subclavian artery just posterior to the angle (right recurrent laryngeal hooks under the artery); the left vagus descends between the left common carotid and subclavian arteries and crosses the aortic arch (left recurrent laryngeal hooks under the arch); the thoracic duct arches over the left subclavian artery to reach the angle

pearl: Injury to the thoracic duct at the left venous angle (neck dissection, left subclavian line) causes chylous leak or chylothorax; the left supraclavicular Virchow node sits nearby.

name: Facial vein
function: Principal vein of the face, draining the forehead, eyelids, nose, lips and cheek. It is valveless and connects the cavernous sinus to the neck, a route for infection spread.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins as the angular vein at the medial canthus; receives deep facial vein (from pterygoid plexus), infraorbital, external nasal, superior and inferior labial, mental, external palatine and submental veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely down and back, behind the facial artery, deep to zygomaticus muscles, crosses the mandible at the anterior border of masseter, then over the submandibular gland

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins anterior division of retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, ending in the IJV

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; communicates with cavernous sinus via superior ophthalmic vein and via deep facial vein and pterygoid plexus

pearl: Danger triangle (nose to angles of mouth): squeezing a furuncle can push infected thrombus via valveless angular and ophthalmic veins into the cavernous sinus, causing cavernous sinus thrombosis.

name: Angular vein
function: Beginning of the facial vein at the medial canthus, formed by the supratrochlear and supraorbital veins; it communicates directly with the superior ophthalmic vein and cavernous sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Union of supratrochlear and supraorbital veins at the root of the nose; receives palpebral and external nasal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs obliquely down the side of the nose along the nasomaxillary groove, lateral to the angular artery, to the level of the inferior orbital margin

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Continues as the facial vein at the inferior orbital margin; connects to the superior ophthalmic vein through the nasofrontal vein at the medial orbit

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies about 8 mm medial to the medial canthus; no valves

pearl: Infections of the upper lip, nose or medial canthus can propagate retrograde through the angular vein into the cavernous sinus; look for ophthalmoplegia (CN III, IV, VI), chemosis and fever.

name: Superior and inferior ophthalmic veins
function: Valveless orbital veins draining the eyeball, orbit and eyelids backward into the cavernous sinus, with anterior connections to the angular/facial vein and inferior connections to the pterygoid plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior: begins at the medial orbit as the continuation of the nasofrontal vein from the angular vein; receives vorticose, central retinal and anterior/posterior ethmoidal veins. Inferior: plexus on the orbital floor

details.label: Course
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein runs back with the ophthalmic artery, crosses the optic nerve and passes through the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus (both); the inferior ophthalmic vein also sends a branch through the inferior orbital fissure to the pterygoid plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: No valves, so blood flows either way depending on pressure

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein (roof of orbit, through the superior orbital fissure to the cavernous sinus); inferior ophthalmic vein (floor of orbit, to the cavernous sinus and pterygoid plexus)

pearl: Carotid-cavernous fistula causes arterialized flow into the superior ophthalmic vein: pulsatile proptosis, chemosis, orbital bruit. A dilated superior ophthalmic vein on CT/MRI is the classic sign.

name: Deep facial vein
function: Short connecting vein running from the pterygoid venous plexus forward over the buccinator to the facial vein, linking the superficial face to the deep infratemporal veins and indirectly to the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises from the anterior part of the pterygoid venous plexus in the infratemporal fossa

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes forward and downward deep to the masseter and ramus, across the buccinator, under the zygomaticus muscles

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein at about the level of the angle of the mouth / anterior border of masseter

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies near the buccal branch of the facial nerve and the parotid duct; valveless

pearl: Second route from face to cavernous sinus: facial vein to deep facial vein to pterygoid plexus to emissary veins of the foramen ovale. Explains cavernous sinus thrombosis after cheek or dental infections.

name: Pterygoid venous plexus
function: Network of veins in the infratemporal fossa between the pterygoid muscles that drains the structures supplied by the maxillary artery (teeth, palate, nasal cavity, muscles of mastication, dura).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins accompanying maxillary artery branches: sphenopalatine, deep temporal, pterygoid, masseteric, buccal, inferior alveolar, posterior superior alveolar, infraorbital, middle meningeal, palatine

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies between temporalis and lateral pterygoid and between the two pterygoid muscles, around the maxillary artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Maxillary vein(s) (to retromandibular vein); communicates with facial vein via deep facial vein, with cavernous sinus via the sphenoidal emissary vein (of Vesalius) and emissary veins of foramen ovale, and with the inferior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral pterygoid muscle, mandibular nerve branches, maxillary artery

pearl: Posterior superior alveolar nerve block or a misplaced needle can pierce the plexus causing a rapidly expanding cheek hematoma. Infections here can track to the cavernous sinus through the foramen ovale.

name: Maxillary vein
function: Short vein that drains the pterygoid venous plexus backward behind the neck of the mandible, where it joins the superficial temporal vein to form the retromandibular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Confluence of veins from the posterior part of the pterygoid venous plexus (the plexus also drains forward into the facial vein via the deep facial vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly with the first part of the maxillary artery between the sphenomandibular ligament and the neck of the mandible

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the superficial temporal vein within the parotid gland to form the retromandibular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies with the maxillary artery deep (medial) to the mandibular neck; auriculotemporal nerve nearby

pearl: Drains the pterygoid plexus, linked to the cavernous sinus via emissary veins (foramen ovale, sphenoidal emissary foramen), so facial/dental infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis; torn by displaced condylar neck fractures.

name: Retromandibular vein
function: Formed in the parotid gland by union of the superficial temporal and maxillary veins; it splits into an anterior division (to the facial vein) and a posterior division (to the external jugular vein).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superficial temporal vein + maxillary vein just behind the neck of the mandible; receives parotid and transverse facial veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends within the parotid gland, superficial to the external carotid artery and deep to the facial nerve branches

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Anterior division joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein (to IJV); posterior division joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Parotid gland layers from superficial to deep: facial nerve, retromandibular vein, external carotid artery

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior division (branch): joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein; posterior division (branch): joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein

pearl: Surgical landmark in parotidectomy: the facial nerve lies just superficial to the retromandibular vein, so the vein marks the plane separating the superficial from the deep lobe of the gland.

name: Common facial vein
function: Short trunk formed by the facial vein and the anterior division of the retromandibular vein below the angle of the mandible; it carries most facial venous blood into the internal jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Facial vein + anterior division of retromandibular vein, just below the angle of the mandible; often receives the lingual and superior thyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Begins just below the angle of the mandible and runs downward and backward across the carotid bifurcation, deep to platysma, to end in the internal jugular vein; the superficial crossing of the submandibular gland is by the facial vein itself, before the union

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein at about the level of the hyoid bone

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses superficial to the carotid bifurcation and hypoglossal nerve; the jugulodigastric lymph node lies close to its termination

pearl: Encountered early in carotid endarterectomy: the common facial vein is divided to expose the carotid bifurcation and the hypoglossal nerve lying just above it.

name: Superficial temporal vein
function: Drains the lateral scalp and temple, descending in front of the tragus to enter the parotid and join the maxillary vein, forming the retromandibular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Frontal and parietal tributaries from the scalp network; receives middle temporal and transverse facial veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends over the zygomatic arch anterior to the tragus with the superficial temporal artery and auriculotemporal nerve, enters the parotid

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins maxillary vein in the parotid to form the retromandibular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies with the auriculotemporal nerve behind the superficial temporal artery; anastomoses freely with supraorbital and posterior auricular veins

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Frontal branch (forehead and anterior scalp); parietal branch (vertex and lateral scalp)

pearl: Scalp lacerations over the temple bleed heavily because the richly anastomotic veins and arteries are held open by the dense connective tissue layer; direct pressure and suturing stop it.

name: Posterior auricular vein
function: Drains the scalp behind the ear and the auricle, descending behind the auricle to join the posterior division of the retromandibular vein and form the external jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Plexus of the scalp behind the ear; receives stylomastoid and auricular veins and the mastoid emissary vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends behind the auricle over the mastoid process and the upper SCM

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the posterior division of the retromandibular vein below the parotid to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompanies the posterior auricular artery; the mastoid emissary vein connects it to the sigmoid sinus

pearl: Mastoid emissary vein links the posterior auricular vein to the sigmoid sinus, so mastoiditis or postauricular infection can lead to sigmoid sinus thrombosis.

name: Occipital vein
function: Drains the posterior scalp, running with the occipital artery to the suboccipital region, where it joins the suboccipital plexus and vertebral vein or the posterior auricular/internal jugular veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Scalp venous plexus over the occiput; receives the occipital emissary vein, the parietal emissary vein and the occipital diploic vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends with the occipital artery, pierces trapezius, enters the suboccipital triangle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus and vertebral vein, or posterior auricular vein / IJV (variable)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Greater occipital nerve accompanies it in the scalp

pearl: Occipital scalp lacerations bleed profusely from this vein and the occipital artery; the parietal and occipital emissary veins allow scalp infection to reach the superior sagittal and transverse sinuses.

name: Lingual vein
function: Drains the tongue and floor of the mouth; the dorsal lingual veins accompany the lingual artery and the deep lingual (ranine) vein runs with the hypoglossal nerve, uniting to enter the IJV.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Dorsal lingual veins (with lingual artery), deep lingual vein of the tongue tip, sublingual vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Deep lingual vein runs back on the underside of the tongue, visible through the mucosa, then with the hypoglossal nerve as the vena comitans nervi hypoglossi on the surface of hyoglossus; the dorsal lingual vein courses medial to hyoglossus with the lingual artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein, directly or via the common facial vein, at the level of the hyoid

details.label: Relations
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve, hyoglossus muscle, greater horn of hyoid

pearl: Sublingual drug absorption (nitroglycerin) is rapid because the deep lingual veins drain into the IJV and bypass first-pass hepatic metabolism.

name: Supraorbital and supratrochlear veins
function: Drain the forehead and anterior scalp downward to the medial canthus, where they unite to form the angular vein; the supraorbital vein also communicates with the superior ophthalmic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Anterior scalp venous network; supraorbital vein also receives the frontal diploic vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Supratrochlear descends near the midline of the forehead; supraorbital runs medially along the orbital rim, sending a branch through the supraorbital notch to the superior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Unite at the medial canthus to form the angular vein; the nasofrontal vein links this junction to the superior ophthalmic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Accompany the supratrochlear and supraorbital nerves and arteries

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Supratrochlear vein (medial forehead, descends near the midline); supraorbital vein (lateral forehead, passes the supraorbital margin)

pearl: Forehead cellulitis or an infected scalp wound can reach the cavernous sinus through the supraorbital-superior ophthalmic connection; the frontal diploic vein links them to the bone and dural sinuses.

name: Superior thyroid vein
function: Drains the upper pole of the thyroid lobe, accompanying the superior thyroid artery to end in the internal jugular vein (or common facial vein).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the upper pole of the thyroid lobe; receives superior laryngeal and cricothyroid veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs upward and laterally with the superior thyroid artery across the external carotid region

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein, or via the common facial vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve runs close to the superior pole vessels

pearl: Ligate the superior pole vessels close to the gland during thyroidectomy to spare the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (cricothyroid), whose injury causes loss of high pitch.

name: Middle thyroid vein
function: Short, often single vein draining the lateral surface of the thyroid lobe directly into the internal jugular vein; it has no accompanying artery.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins from the lateral and inferior part of the thyroid lobe

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes laterally across the common carotid artery at the level of the cricoid

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies anterior to the common carotid artery; tethers the thyroid lobe to the IJV

pearl: The middle thyroid vein must be divided early when mobilizing the thyroid lobe medially; avulsion from the IJV causes brisk bleeding or air embolism.

name: Inferior thyroid veins
function: Several veins from the lower poles and isthmus that form a plexus in front of the trachea and descend behind the manubrium to the brachiocephalic veins; they do not follow the inferior thyroid artery.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Pretracheal venous plexus from the isthmus and lower poles; receive inferior laryngeal, tracheal and esophageal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Descend on the front of the trachea behind the strap muscles, through the suprasternal region into the superior mediastinum, often uniting as a common trunk

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Left vein into the left brachiocephalic vein; right vein into the right brachiocephalic vein (or at its junction with the SVC)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lie in front of the trachea below the isthmus and are crossed in tracheostomy; a thyroid ima artery (about 10%) may ascend among them

pearl: Bleeding risks in tracheostomy and thyroidectomy: inferior thyroid veins, thyroid ima artery and jugular venous arch lie in front of the trachea below the isthmus; stay midline, open the trachea at rings 2-3, not lower.

name: Vertebral vein
function: Forms as a plexus around the vertebral artery in the transverse foramina of C1-C6, draining the suboccipital region and deep neck muscles, and emerges at C6 to end in the brachiocephalic vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus and veins from the internal vertebral venous plexus, deep cervical muscles and occipital vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends as a plexus around the vertebral artery through the transverse foramina of C1-C6 (the C7 transverse foramen transmits vertebral veins but usually not the artery), then as a single vein anterior to the first part of the subclavian artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Posterior aspect of the brachiocephalic vein near the venous angle

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical vein joins it; lies anterior to the vertebral artery in the lower neck

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Venous plexus around the vertebral artery (in the transverse foramina); vertebral vein proper (single trunk below C6); anterior vertebral vein (with the ascending cervical artery); accessory vertebral vein (through the C7 transverse foramen); deep cervical vein (from the suboccipital region, joins near termination)

pearl: Part of Batson's valveless vertebral venous plexus, linked to the intracranial sinuses via the condylar emissary vein: retrograde flow with raised intrathoracic or abdominal pressure lets prostate and breast cancer seed the vertebrae and skull base, and lets infection spread to the spine or dural sinuses.

name: Vertebral venous plexus (Batson)
function: Valveless network of internal (epidural) and external vertebral veins from skull base to sacrum, communicating with the dural sinuses and the vertebral, intercostal, lumbar and pelvic veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Internal plexus in the epidural space (anterior and posterior longitudinal channels) + external plexus around vertebral bodies and arches; basivertebral veins from the bodies

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs the full length of the vertebral canal; communicates superiorly with the basilar and occipital sinuses and the condylar emissary veins

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Vertebral veins (neck), intercostal, lumbar and lateral sacral veins; thus links the caval and azygos systems with the pelvic (prostatic, vesical) venous plexuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: No valves, so flow reverses with raised intrathoracic or intra-abdominal pressure (coughing, straining, Valsalva)

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Internal vertebral (epidural) venous plexus (anterior and posterior, inside the vertebral canal); external vertebral venous plexus (anterior on the bodies, posterior on the arches); basivertebral veins (from the vertebral bodies into the anterior internal plexus); intervertebral veins (through the intervertebral foramina to the vertebral and segmental veins)

pearl: Batson plexus explains hematogenous spread of prostate (and breast) cancer to the vertebral bodies and skull without lung metastases, and spread of pelvic/urinary infection to the spine (vertebral osteomyelitis, epidural abscess).

name: Cavernous sinus
function: Paired trabeculated dural venous sinus on each side of the sella turcica that drains the orbit, face and brain and surrounds the ICA and cranial nerves III, IV, V1, V2 and VI.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior and inferior ophthalmic veins, superficial middle cerebral vein (via sphenoparietal sinus), central retinal vein, efferent hypophyseal veins; connects to pterygoid plexus via the sphenoidal emissary vein (of Vesalius) and emissary veins of foramen ovale

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies lateral to the sella and sphenoid body, from the superior orbital fissure to the petrous apex; the two sides join via intercavernous sinuses around the pituitary

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior petrosal sinus (to transverse sinus) and inferior petrosal sinus (to IJV at jugular foramen); basilar plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: ICA and abducens nerve (VI) run through the sinus; III, IV, V1 and V2 lie in its lateral wall; pituitary medial, temporal lobe lateral

pearl: Cavernous sinus thrombosis (sinusitis, danger-triangle/orbital infection): fever, headache, proptosis/chemosis, ophthalmoplegia (VI first), V1/V2 numbness; often bilateral. IV anti-staph antibiotics; usually add heparin.

name: Superior sagittal sinus
function: Midline dural sinus in the attached border of the falx cerebri, running from the crista galli to the confluence; it receives superior cerebral veins and is the main site of CSF absorption via arachnoid granulations.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior cerebral (bridging) veins, frontal diploic vein, parietal emissary veins and an emissary vein through the foramen cecum; lateral venous lacunae (of Trolard) containing arachnoid granulations

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward in the midline groove of the skull vault from the foramen cecum to the internal occipital protuberance, widening posteriorly

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Confluence of sinuses, usually continuing as the right transverse sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Bridging veins enter it against the direction of flow; parietal emissary veins connect it to the scalp

pearl: Torn bridging veins entering the sinus cause subdural hematoma (elderly, alcoholics, shaken infants). Sinus thrombosis (OCPs, pregnancy/postpartum, thrombophilia): headache, seizures, papilledema; diagnose with MR/CT venography and anticoagulate even if hemorrhagic.

name: Transverse and sigmoid sinuses
function: Paired sinuses carrying blood from the confluence laterally along the tentorium (transverse) and then in an S-shaped groove on the mastoid (sigmoid) to the jugular foramen, where the IJV begins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Transverse: from the confluence, receives superior petrosal sinus, inferior cerebral veins, inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé) and inferior cerebellar veins. Sigmoid: continuation of transverse, receives mastoid and condylar emissary veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Transverse sinus runs laterally in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli; sigmoid curves down and medially behind the mastoid antrum to the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen

details.label: Relations
details.value: Right transverse sinus is usually the larger, continuing the superior sagittal sinus; sigmoid sinus lies just behind the mastoid air cells and the facial nerve canal

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Transverse sinus (in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli, from the confluence to the petrous base); sigmoid sinus (continuation of the transverse sinus, S-shaped groove to the jugular foramen)

pearl: Mastoiditis or otitis media can erode into the sigmoid sinus causing septic lateral sinus thrombosis (Griesinger sign: mastoid edema). The sinus is at risk in mastoidectomy and posterior fossa craniotomy.

name: Confluence of sinuses (torcular herophili)
function: Dilated junction at the internal occipital protuberance where the superior sagittal, straight and occipital sinuses meet and divide into the two transverse sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus, straight sinus, occipital sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies against the internal occipital protuberance, deep to the inion

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Right and left transverse sinuses (commonly superior sagittal to right, straight to left; often asymmetric)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Attachment of falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli; occipital bone posteriorly

pearl: A suboccipital craniotomy or a depressed fracture over the inion can lacerate the confluence, producing torrential venous bleeding; asymmetric transverse sinuses are common and must not be mistaken for thrombosis.

name: Straight sinus and great cerebral vein (of Galen)
function: Great cerebral vein collects the deep cerebral veins (internal cerebral and basal veins) draining thalamus and basal ganglia; with the inferior sagittal sinus it forms the straight sinus, which runs to the confluence.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Great cerebral vein = union of the two internal cerebral veins, receiving the basal veins of Rosenthal, dorsal vein of the corpus callosum, internal occipital veins and superior vermian vein; straight sinus = great cerebral vein + inferior sagittal sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Great cerebral vein curves up behind the splenium; straight sinus runs posteroinferiorly in the junction of the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Confluence of sinuses, usually continuing as the left transverse sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Great cerebral vein lies in the quadrigeminal cistern above the pineal gland and superior colliculi

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Great cerebral vein (of Galen) (short midline trunk formed by the two internal cerebral veins, receives the basal veins); straight sinus (in the junction of falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli, formed by the great cerebral vein and inferior sagittal sinus)

pearl: Vein of Galen malformation in neonates causes high-output heart failure, cranial bruit and hydrocephalus. Deep cerebral venous thrombosis causes bilateral thalamic edema with depressed consciousness.

name: Emissary veins
function: Valveless veins passing through skull foramina to connect the extracranial scalp and face veins with the intracranial dural sinuses; they equalize pressure but allow infection to spread inward.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Parietal (scalp to superior sagittal sinus), foramen cecum (nasal/frontal veins to superior sagittal sinus), mastoid (posterior auricular to sigmoid sinus), condylar (suboccipital plexus to sigmoid sinus), sphenoidal emissary vein of Vesalius and foramen ovale (pterygoid plexus to cavernous sinus), occipital (occipital vein to confluence region)

details.label: Course
details.value: Pass through the parietal foramen, mastoid foramen, condylar canal, sphenoidal emissary foramen (of Vesalius), foramen ovale and foramen cecum

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Dural venous sinuses from the scalp, face and pterygoid plexus; flow may reverse

details.label: Relations
details.value: Connect the loose areolar (danger) layer of the scalp to the sinuses

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Parietal emissary vein (parietal foramen, to superior sagittal sinus); mastoid emissary vein (mastoid foramen, to sigmoid sinus); occipital emissary vein (near the external occipital protuberance, to the confluence of sinuses); condylar emissary vein (condylar canal, to sigmoid sinus); sphenoidal emissary vein of Vesalius (sphenoidal emissary foramen, cavernous sinus to pterygoid plexus); emissary vein of the foramen cecum (to superior sagittal sinus)

pearl: Infection in the loose connective tissue layer of the scalp spreads via emissary veins to the dural sinuses and meninges (osteomyelitis, sinus thrombosis, meningitis); hence the scalp 'danger area'.

name: Diploic veins
function: Thin-walled, valveless veins within the cancellous diploe of the skull vault (frontal, anterior and posterior temporal, occipital) that drain into both the dural sinuses and the scalp/pericranial veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Frontal diploic vein, anterior and posterior temporal diploic veins, occipital diploic vein, each draining a region of the vault

details.label: Course
details.value: Run in channels within the diploe between the inner and outer tables of the skull

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Inward to the superior sagittal, sphenoparietal, transverse sinuses; outward to supraorbital, deep temporal and occipital veins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Become prominent on skull X-ray as branching lucencies; connect with emissary veins

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Frontal diploic vein (to supraorbital vein and superior sagittal sinus); anterior temporal diploic vein (to sphenoparietal sinus and deep temporal veins); posterior temporal diploic vein (to transverse sinus); occipital diploic vein (to occipital vein or transverse sinus)

pearl: Osteomyelitis of the frontal bone from sinusitis (Pott puffy tumor) spreads via diploic veins to cause subperiosteal abscess, epidural abscess and superior sagittal sinus thrombosis.

name: Scalp veins
function: Richly anastomotic superficial scalp veins (supratrochlear, supraorbital, superficial temporal, posterior auricular, occipital) in the dense connective tissue layer, linked to dural sinuses by emissary veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Network over the vault drained by the supratrochlear, supraorbital, superficial temporal, posterior auricular and occipital veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Lie in the dense subcutaneous connective tissue (layer 2 of SCALP) with the arteries; emissary veins pass from the loose areolar layer (layer 4) through the skull to the sinuses

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein (anteriorly), retromandibular and external jugular veins (laterally), suboccipital plexus/vertebral vein and IJV via occipital veins (posteriorly)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Walls are held open by dense connective tissue; the loose areolar layer lets blood or pus spread across the vault and into the eyelids (periorbital ecchymosis)

pearl: Scalp wounds bleed profusely because the vessels cannot retract. Subgaleal hematoma or infection in the loose areolar layer spreads over the whole vault into the eyelids, and via emissary veins to the dural sinuses and meninges.

name: Inferior petrosal sinus
function: Main outflow of the cavernous sinus: runs posteroinferiorly along the petro-occipital fissure to the superior bulb of the internal jugular vein at the jugular foramen.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises from the posteroinferior cavernous sinus; receives labyrinthine (internal auditory) veins, pontine and medullary veins, and the basilar plexus

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteroinferiorly in the groove between the petrous temporal bone and basilar occiput (petro-occipital fissure) to the anterior part of the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein just below the jugular foramen (sometimes joins the sigmoid sinus or jugular bulb directly)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Traverses the anterior (pars nervosa) compartment of the jugular foramen alongside CN IX; the basilar plexus on the clivus links the two inferior petrosal sinuses

pearl: Bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (central:peripheral ACTH ratio ≥2 basal, ≥3 after CRH) confirms pituitary Cushing disease vs ectopic ACTH when pituitary MRI is negative or equivocal (<6 mm) in ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome.

name: Superior petrosal sinus
function: Runs along the petrous ridge in the attached margin of the tentorium, connecting the cavernous sinus to the junction of the transverse and sigmoid sinuses; a key channel linking anterior and posterior dural sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the posterosuperior cavernous sinus; receives cerebellar, inferior cerebral and tympanic veins, plus the petrosal vein (of Dandy) from the cerebellum/brainstem

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes posterolaterally in the attached edge of the tentorium cerebelli, grooving the superior border of the petrous temporal bone, and arches over the trigeminal root

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Transverse sinus at the point where it turns into the sigmoid sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses above the trigeminal nerve at the petrous apex (Meckel cave) and lies near the superior semicircular canal and arcuate eminence

pearl: Cavernous sinus thrombosis spreads posteriorly via the petrosal sinuses to the transverse/sigmoid sinuses; otitis media/mastoiditis can seed the same path in reverse. Treat with IV antibiotics plus anticoagulation.

name: Bridging (superior cerebral) veins
function: Eight to twelve veins per hemisphere draining the superolateral and medial cortex; they cross the subarachnoid and subdural spaces to empty into the superior sagittal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Converge from cortical pial veins of the frontal, parietal and occipital lobes; the largest is the superior anastomotic vein of Trolard linking to the superficial middle cerebral vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascend over the convexity, pierce the arachnoid, traverse the subdural space and enter the dura on the lateral wall of the superior sagittal sinus; posterior veins enter obliquely forward against the direction of flow

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus (directly or via the lateral venous lacunae), then confluence and transverse sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Unsupported segment in the subdural space is thin-walled and fixed at the sinus, so it tears with acceleration-deceleration or cerebral atrophy that stretches the veins

pearl: Torn bridging veins cause subdural hematoma: crescent-shaped, crosses sutures but not the midline; classic with cerebral atrophy (elderly, alcoholics), anticoagulation, and shaken infants (retinal hemorrhages).

name: Inferior sagittal sinus
function: Small sinus in the free inferior edge of the falx cerebri that drains the medial hemispheres and falx and joins the great cerebral vein of Galen to form the straight sinus, completing the deep venous pathway.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins near the junction of the anterior and middle thirds of the falx; receives veins from the falx, corpus callosum, cingulate gyrus and medial surfaces of the hemispheres

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs posteriorly in the posterior half to two-thirds of the free margin of the falx cerebri, above the corpus callosum, enlarging as it goes

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Unites with the great cerebral vein of Galen at the falx-tentorium junction to form the straight sinus, which runs to the confluence of sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the two hemispheres directly above the corpus callosum and pericallosal arteries; the deep system (internal cerebral veins, basal veins, vein of Galen) enters at its termination

pearl: Deep cerebral venous thrombosis (straight sinus, vein of Galen) causes bilateral thalamic edema with coma; suspect with OCPs, pregnancy/puerperium or thrombophilia; confirm with MR/CT venography.

name: Sphenoparietal sinus
function: Small dural sinus running medially along the posterior edge of the lesser wing of the sphenoid; it carries the superficial middle cerebral vein into the anterior end of the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superficial middle cerebral vein (from the lateral cerebral sulcus), meningeal veins of the anterior part of the middle cranial fossa, diploic veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Along the under-surface of the lesser wing of the sphenoid, from the pterion region medially toward the anterior clinoid process

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Anterior part of the cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the dura at the junction of the anterior and middle cranial fossae; the middle meningeal vessels run just posterior to its lateral end

pearl: A route by which superficial cortical veins of the frontal and temporal lobes drain into the cavernous sinus, so cavernous sinus thrombosis can back up into cortical veins and cause venous infarction or hemorrhage with seizures.

name: Occipital sinus
function: Smallest of the dural venous sinuses; runs in the attached margin of the falx cerebelli from the margin of the foramen magnum up to the confluence of sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Marginal sinuses around the foramen magnum, which communicate with the internal vertebral venous plexus (of Batson) and the sigmoid sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Ascends in the midline of the posterior cranial fossa within the attached border of the falx cerebelli, grooving the internal occipital crest

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Confluence of sinuses (torcular herophili)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Overlies the cerebellar vermis; adjacent to the inferior vermian and inferior cerebellar hemispheric veins

pearl: Its connection with the vertebral venous plexus around the foramen magnum is one of the valveless routes by which pelvic or prostate cancer can seed the skull base and posterior fossa; a large occipital sinus is also a bleeding hazard in midline suboccipital craniotomy.

name: Basilar venous plexus
function: Network of dural veins on the clivus connecting the two inferior petrosal sinuses and the cavernous sinuses with the internal vertebral venous plexus through the foramen magnum.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cavernous sinuses (via the posterior intercavernous sinus), inferior petrosal sinuses, veins of the clivus

details.label: Course
details.value: Spreads over the basilar part of the occipital bone (clivus) behind the dorsum sellae, between the layers of dura, down to the foramen magnum

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Inferior petrosal sinuses, marginal sinus and the internal (epidural) vertebral venous plexus; the whole system is valveless

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies between the clivus and the pons and medulla, in front of the basilar artery; the abducens nerves ascend through it toward the petrous apex (Dorello canal)

pearl: Valveless link between the cavernous sinus and Batson's vertebral plexus: a pathway by which sinus infection or thrombosis can spread caudally and by which pelvic tumor emboli can reach the skull base without passing through the lungs.

name: Anterior and posterior intercavernous sinuses
function: Transverse dural channels in front of and behind the pituitary stalk that join the right and left cavernous sinuses, forming a venous ring (circular sinus) around the hypophysis.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Efferent hypophyseal veins from the pituitary gland; veins of the diaphragma sellae

details.label: Course
details.value: Run across the midline within the diaphragma sellae and the dura of the sella, anterior and posterior to the infundibulum; the posterior sinus continues onto the clivus as the basilar venous plexus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus of each side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Immediately above and around the pituitary gland, below the optic chiasm; crossed during transsphenoidal surgery

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Anterior intercavernous sinus (in front of the infundibulum); posterior intercavernous sinus (behind the infundibulum, continuous with the basilar venous plexus)

pearl: Because the two cavernous sinuses communicate through these channels, septic thrombosis that starts on one side (danger triangle, sinusitis) commonly becomes bilateral within days; the anterior intercavernous sinus is the usual source of venous bleeding when the dura of the sella is opened in transsphenoidal pituitary surgery.

name: Superficial middle cerebral vein
function: Large superficial vein lying in the lateral (sylvian) sulcus that drains most of the lateral surface of the hemisphere into the sphenoparietal and cavernous sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the frontal, parietal and temporal opercula around the lateral sulcus; connected to the superior sagittal sinus by the superior anastomotic vein (of Trolard) and to the transverse sinus by the inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé)

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and downward along the lateral sulcus beneath the arachnoid, then medially along the lesser wing of the sphenoid

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Sphenoparietal sinus, then the cavernous sinus (sometimes directly into the cavernous sinus or, via an emissary vein, the pterygoid plexus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: The deep middle cerebral vein lies in the depth of the same sulcus on the insula and drains instead into the basal vein (of Rosenthal)

pearl: Thrombosis of the cortical veins that feed it (pregnancy, OCPs, dehydration, thrombophilia) causes headache with focal deficits or seizures and hemorrhagic venous infarction that does not follow an arterial territory; diagnose with MR or CT venography.

name: Superior (Trolard) and inferior (Labbé) anastomotic veins
function: Two inconstant cortical veins that link the superficial middle cerebral vein with the superior sagittal sinus above and the transverse sinus below, providing collateral venous drainage of the lateral hemisphere.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the lateral convexity; both begin from the superficial middle cerebral vein in the lateral sulcus

details.label: Course
details.value: Trolard: ascends across the frontoparietal convexity to the superior sagittal sinus. Labbé: runs posteroinferiorly across the temporal lobe to the transverse sinus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus (Trolard); transverse sinus near its junction with the sigmoid sinus (Labbé)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Usually one is dominant; the vein of Labbé is typically the larger on the dominant (left) hemisphere

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior anastomotic vein (of Trolard) (superficial middle cerebral vein to superior sagittal sinus); inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé) (superficial middle cerebral vein to transverse sinus)

pearl: The vein of Labbé is the main venous outflow of the temporal lobe: sacrificing it during temporal craniotomy or thrombosing it with transverse sinus thrombosis causes temporal lobe venous infarction with aphasia (left) and hemorrhage; bridging veins like these tear in subdural hematoma.

name: Internal cerebral veins and basal vein (of Rosenthal)
function: Paired deep veins of the brain: the internal cerebral veins drain the deep gray matter and ventricular walls, the basal veins drain the base of the hemisphere; both unite to form the great cerebral vein (of Galen).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Internal cerebral vein: superior thalamostriate vein, superior choroid vein and vein of the septum pellucidum, uniting at the interventricular foramen (of Monro); also veins of the caudate nucleus and thalamus. Basal vein: anterior cerebral vein, deep middle cerebral vein and inferior thalamostriate veins near the optic chiasm, later joined by the posterior mesencephalic and hippocampal/inferior ventricular veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Internal cerebral veins run backward side by side in the tela choroidea of the roof of the 3rd ventricle. The basal vein curves around the cerebral peduncle (crus cerebri) between the optic tract and the parahippocampal gyrus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Both pairs join beneath the splenium of the corpus callosum to form the great cerebral vein (of Galen), which enters the straight sinus with the inferior sagittal sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Internal cerebral veins lie above the thalamus and below the fornix; the basal vein accompanies the posterior cerebral artery around the midbrain

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Internal cerebral vein (right and left, in the roof of the 3rd ventricle; formed by the superior thalamostriate, superior choroid and septum pellucidum veins); basal vein (of Rosenthal) (around the cerebral crus; formed by the anterior cerebral, deep middle cerebral and inferior thalamostriate veins)

pearl: Deep cerebral venous thrombosis (internal cerebral veins, vein of Galen, straight sinus) causes bilateral thalamic edema with coma, decreased consciousness and no lateralizing signs; look for the hyperdense vein and thalamic hypodensity on CT in a hypercoagulable or postpartum patient. A vein of Galen malformation presents in neonates with high-output heart failure and a cranial bruit.

name: Middle meningeal veins
function: Veins that accompany the frontal and parietal branches of the middle meningeal artery between the dura and the skull, draining the dura and the diploe and leaving the skull through the foramen spinosum.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Meningeal veins of the dura, diploic veins; communicate with the superior sagittal sinus via the lateral (venous) lacunae and with the sphenoparietal sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Run with the middle meningeal artery in the grooves of the inner table of the parietal and squamous temporal bones; the veins lie between the artery and the bone

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Pterygoid venous plexus through the foramen spinosum (with the middle meningeal artery); also the cavernous sinus and sphenoparietal sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: The pterion overlies the frontal (anterior) branch; the trunk passes through the foramen spinosum with the meningeal branch of the mandibular nerve

pearl: A pterion fracture usually tears the middle meningeal artery, but the accompanying vein can be the source of a slower, venous epidural hematoma, typically in the temporal region, without the classic lucid interval; venous epidurals also occur from torn dural sinuses at the vertex and posterior fossa.

name: Nasofrontal vein
function: Short vein at the medial orbital margin that connects the angular vein (from the face) with the superior ophthalmic vein (to the cavernous sinus).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of the angular vein at the medial canthus; also receives the supratrochlear and supraorbital veins near the medial end of the eyebrow

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes backward through the medial orbital margin above the medial palpebral ligament into the orbit

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein, and through it the cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless like the rest of the facial-orbital venous route; lies near the trochlea and the origin of the supraorbital vein

pearl: This is the exact link in the danger-triangle pathway: angular vein to nasofrontal vein to superior ophthalmic vein to cavernous sinus, so a squeezed nasal or upper-lip furuncle can seed septic cavernous sinus thrombosis.

name: Sphenoidal emissary vein (of Vesalius)
function: Inconstant emissary vein passing through the sphenoidal emissary foramen (of Vesalius), medial to the foramen ovale, to connect the cavernous sinus with the pterygoid venous plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises from the anterior-inferior part of the cavernous sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends through the sphenoidal emissary foramen in the greater wing of the sphenoid, anteromedial to the foramen ovale (present in a minority of skulls, often unilateral)

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Pterygoid venous plexus in the infratemporal fossa; flow can go in either direction because there are no valves

details.label: Relations
details.value: Other emissary veins of the middle fossa pass through the foramen ovale and foramen lacerum to the same plexus

pearl: Allows infection from a dental abscess, deep face or a contaminated pterygoid-plexus needle (posterior superior alveolar block) to pass upward into the cavernous sinus; the foramen can be mistaken for a fracture or an abnormal lesion on skull-base CT.

name: Submental vein
function: Vein that accompanies the submental artery beneath the chin, draining the floor of the mouth, anterior belly of digastric, mylohyoid and submental skin into the facial vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the submental skin, mylohyoid and anterior belly of digastric; communicates with the sublingual vein and the anterior jugular vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward on the mylohyoid muscle below the lower border of the mandible, superficial to the submandibular gland, with the submental artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein just before the facial vein crosses the submandibular gland (sometimes the anterior jugular vein instead)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Submental lymph nodes lie along it; the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve runs just above the lower border of the mandible lateral to it

pearl: Bleeding and submental swelling after floor-of-mouth procedures track along this vein; in Ludwig angina the submental space is one of the three spaces (submandibular, sublingual, submental) that become board-hard and threaten the airway.

name: Superior laryngeal vein
function: Vein draining the supraglottic larynx that accompanies the superior laryngeal artery and internal laryngeal nerve through the thyrohyoid membrane and empties into the superior thyroid vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the laryngeal vestibule, epiglottis, aryepiglottic folds and piriform recess mucosa

details.label: Course
details.value: Leaves the larynx through the opening in the thyrohyoid membrane with the superior laryngeal artery and the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior thyroid vein, then the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: The inferior laryngeal vein, by contrast, drains the subglottis with the recurrent laryngeal nerve into the inferior thyroid veins

pearl: Supraglottic laryngeal cancers (epiglottis, false cords) drain by lymphatics that travel with this vein through the thyrohyoid membrane to the upper deep cervical (level II-III) nodes, so they present with nodes early and bilaterally, unlike glottic tumors.

name: Pharyngeal venous plexus
function: Network of veins on the posterior and lateral surface of the pharyngeal constrictors that drains the pharynx, soft palate and auditory tube into the internal jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the pharyngeal wall, prevertebral muscles, soft palate and the pharyngeal end of the auditory tube; communicates above with the pterygoid plexus and cavernous sinus and below with the laryngeal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies in the buccopharyngeal fascia on the outer surface of the constrictors, in front of the prevertebral fascia and retropharyngeal space

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Pharyngeal veins that end in the internal jugular vein (occasionally the facial, lingual or superior thyroid veins)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Sympathetic trunk and superior cervical ganglion lie posterolateral to it; the retropharyngeal nodes are embedded nearby

pearl: Septic thrombophlebitis of this plexus and the adjacent internal jugular vein after tonsillitis or a peritonsillar abscess is Lemierre syndrome (Fusobacterium necrophorum) with septic pulmonary emboli; pharyngeal veins also bleed heavily when a retropharyngeal abscess is drained.

name: Vorticose veins
function: Four to five veins that pierce the sclera behind the equator of the eyeball to drain the choroid, ciliary body and iris into the ophthalmic veins.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Suprachoroidal tributaries from the choroidal venous layer, with the veins of the ciliary body and iris; they anastomose with the episcleral veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Converge in a whorl (vortex) in the choroid and pierce the sclera obliquely between the recti, about 6 mm behind the equator, one in each quadrant

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein (upper pair) and inferior ophthalmic vein (lower pair), then the cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: The anterior ciliary veins separately drain the scleral venous sinus (canal of Schlemm) and the anterior segment

pearl: Vorticose veins are the venous outflow of the uveal tract: raised cavernous sinus pressure (carotid-cavernous fistula, cavernous sinus thrombosis) or extreme venous congestion causes choroidal effusion and raised intraocular pressure; they must be avoided in scleral buckling and strabismus surgery because a torn vorticose vein causes choroidal hemorrhage.

name: Efferent hypophyseal veins and hypophyseal portal veins
function: Venous outflow of the pituitary gland: short efferent hypophyseal veins pass from both lobes into the cavernous and intercavernous sinuses, while the hypophyseal portal veins carry hypothalamic releasing hormones from the median eminence to the anterior lobe.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Primary capillary plexus of the hypophyseal portal system in the infundibulum and median eminence (fed by the superior hypophyseal artery) drains into long portal veins down the stalk, which form the secondary plexus in the anterior lobe; the capillary plexus of the infundibular process and posterior lobe is fed by the inferior hypophyseal artery

details.label: Course
details.value: Portal veins run along the pituitary stalk; the efferent veins leave the lateral surfaces of both lobes

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus on each side and the anterior and posterior intercavernous sinuses, then the inferior petrosal sinuses to the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Pituitary hormones therefore enter the systemic circulation through the cavernous and inferior petrosal sinuses

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Primary plexus of the hypophyseal portal system (infundibulum and median eminence); portal veins of hypophysis (down the stalk); secondary plexus of the hypophyseal portal system (anterior lobe); capillary plexus of the infundibular process (posterior lobe); efferent hypophyseal veins (to the cavernous sinus)

pearl: Inferior petrosal sinus sampling after CRH stimulation reads this venous outflow: a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient (>2 basal or >3 after CRH) confirms Cushing disease and distinguishes it from ectopic ACTH when the MRI is equivocal. Pituitary stalk transection (trauma, surgery) interrupts the portal veins and causes anterior hypopituitarism with hyperprolactinemia.

name: Anterior division (branch) of retromandibular vein
function: Anterior of the two terminal branches of the retromandibular vein; it carries blood from the superficial temporal and maxillary territories forward to the facial vein and so into the internal jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises where the retromandibular vein divides at the lower pole of the parotid gland, near the angle of the mandible

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and downward below the angle of the mandible, superficial to the external carotid artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the facial vein to form the common facial vein, which ends in the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Emerges from the lower pole of the parotid; lies near the marginal mandibular and cervical branches of the facial nerve and the submandibular gland

pearl: The divisions decide where parotid and scalp blood ends up: anterior division to the internal jugular system, posterior division to the external jugular vein.

name: Posterior division (branch) of retromandibular vein
function: Posterior of the two terminal branches of the retromandibular vein; it unites with the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Arises where the retromandibular vein divides at the lower pole of the parotid gland, near the angle of the mandible

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes backward and downward from the parotid onto the surface of the sternocleidomastoid muscle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lower pole of the parotid gland, angle of the mandible, great auricular nerve on sternocleidomastoid

name: Superior bulb of internal jugular vein
function: Dilated beginning of the internal jugular vein in the jugular fossa, where it receives the sigmoid sinus; it lies directly beneath the floor of the middle ear.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of the sigmoid sinus at the jugular foramen; the inferior petrosal sinus joins at or just below it

details.label: Course
details.value: Occupies the jugular fossa of the temporal bone in the posterior part of the jugular foramen, then continues down as the internal jugular vein in the carotid sheath

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Floor of the tympanic cavity above; CN IX, X and XI leave the jugular foramen anteromedial to it; internal carotid artery in front

pearl: A high or dehiscent jugular bulb appears as a blue mass behind the tympanic membrane and causes pulsatile tinnitus; glomus jugulare tumors arise in its wall and can produce jugular foramen syndrome (CN IX, X, XI palsies).

name: Inferior bulb of internal jugular vein
function: Dilation at the lower end of the internal jugular vein just above its union with the subclavian vein; a bicuspid valve above it limits reflux of blood toward the head.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Lower end of the internal jugular vein; the external jugular and vertebral veins end close by

details.label: Course
details.value: Lies deep to the interval between the sternal and clavicular heads of sternocleidomastoid (lesser supraclavicular fossa), behind the medial end of the clavicle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the subclavian vein at the venous angle to form the brachiocephalic vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Common carotid artery and vagus nerve medial; cervical pleura and first part of the subclavian artery behind; thoracic duct (left) or right lymphatic duct enters at the angle

pearl: Target of the low (central) approach to internal jugular catheterization between the two heads of sternocleidomastoid; the nearby pleura and, on the left, the thoracic duct are at risk.

name: Superior labial vein
function: Drains the upper lip and adjacent nasal septum and ala into the facial vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network of the upper lip; communicates across the midline and with the external nasal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally in the upper lip with the superior labial artery, between orbicularis oris and the mucosa

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein near the angle of the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superior labial artery, orbicularis oris, labial glands

pearl: Lies in the danger triangle of the face: infection of the upper lip and nose can reach the cavernous sinus through the valveless facial, angular and ophthalmic veins.

name: Inferior labial vein
function: Drains the lower lip into the facial vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network of the lower lip; communicates with the mental vein and the vein of the opposite side

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally in the lower lip with the inferior labial artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein below the angle of the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior labial artery, orbicularis oris, depressor anguli oris

name: External palatine (paratonsillar) vein
function: Drains the soft palate and the tonsillar bed downward across the lateral surface of the palatine tonsil to the facial vein or pharyngeal venous plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Veins of the soft palate and palatine tonsil

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends from the soft palate on the lateral surface of the tonsillar capsule, then pierces the superior pharyngeal constrictor

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Facial vein (or the pharyngeal venous plexus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tonsillar bed (superior constrictor), palatine tonsil, tonsillar branch of the facial artery

pearl: The usual source of venous bleeding after tonsillectomy, because it runs in the tonsillar bed just lateral to the capsule.

name: Superior ophthalmic vein
function: Main vein of the orbit: drains the eyeball, upper orbit and eyelids backward into the cavernous sinus and communicates in front with the angular vein, linking the face to the intracranial sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the medial angle of the orbit from the nasofrontal vein (from the supraorbital, supratrochlear and angular veins); receives the superior vorticose veins, central retinal vein, lacrimal and ethmoidal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward with the ophthalmic artery beneath the superior rectus, crosses above the optic nerve and leaves through the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; passes through the superior orbital fissure outside (above) the common tendinous ring

pearl: A dilated superior ophthalmic vein on CT or MRI with pulsatile proptosis, chemosis and an orbital bruit indicates a carotid-cavernous fistula; the vein also carries facial infection to the cavernous sinus.

name: Inferior ophthalmic vein
function: Drains the floor of the orbit, the inferior extraocular muscles and the lower part of the eyeball to the cavernous sinus, with a communication to the pterygoid venous plexus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Venous network on the floor and medial wall of the orbit; receives the inferior vorticose veins and veins of the inferior rectus, inferior oblique and lower eyelid

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs backward on the inferior rectus along the floor of the orbit

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Cavernous sinus, directly or by joining the superior ophthalmic vein; a branch passes through the inferior orbital fissure to the pterygoid plexus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Valveless; inferior rectus, infraorbital vessels and nerve, inferior orbital fissure

name: Central retinal vein
function: Sole venous drainage of the inner retina: the retinal venules converge on the optic disc and leave the eye within the optic nerve.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Superior and inferior nasal, temporal and macular retinal venules, uniting at the optic disc

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs in the optic nerve alongside the central retinal artery, then leaves the nerve behind the eyeball and crosses the subarachnoid space

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior ophthalmic vein or directly into the cavernous sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Central retinal artery within the optic nerve and lamina cribrosa of the sclera

pearl: Central retinal vein occlusion causes sudden painless monocular vision loss with diffuse retinal hemorrhages, dilated tortuous veins and disc edema (blood and thunder fundus); raised intracranial pressure compresses the vein and abolishes venous pulsation, contributing to papilledema.

name: Deep cervical vein
function: Drains the suboccipital region and the deep muscles of the back of the neck, accompanying the deep cervical artery down to the vertebral vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus, occipital vein and veins of the deep posterior neck muscles; communicates with the venous plexus around the vertebral artery

details.label: Course
details.value: Descends between semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis, then passes forward between the C7 transverse process and the neck of the first rib

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Lower end of the vertebral vein (or the brachiocephalic vein)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep cervical artery, semispinalis muscles, costocervical trunk

name: Transverse sinus
function: Paired dural sinus that carries blood from the confluence of sinuses laterally along the occipital bone to the sigmoid sinus; the right usually continues the superior sagittal sinus and the left the straight sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Begins at the confluence of sinuses; receives the superior petrosal sinus, inferior cerebral veins, inferior anastomotic vein (of Labbé), inferior cerebellar veins and diploic veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs laterally and forward in the attached margin of the tentorium cerebelli, in the groove for the transverse sinus of the occipital bone, to the base of the petrous temporal bone

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Continues as the sigmoid sinus where the superior petrosal sinus joins

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli; occipital lobe above and cerebellum below; the right sinus is usually the larger

pearl: Transverse sinus thrombosis (often from otitis media or mastoiditis, or in hypercoagulable states) presents with headache and papilledema and can cause temporal lobe venous infarction through the vein of Labbé; a hypoplastic left sinus is a common normal variant on MR venography.

name: Sigmoid sinus
function: S-shaped continuation of the transverse sinus that descends behind the mastoid to the jugular foramen, where it becomes the internal jugular vein; the final common pathway for most intracranial venous blood.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Continuation of the transverse sinus; receives the mastoid and condylar emissary veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Curves downward and medially in the sigmoid groove of the temporal and occipital bones, then turns forward to the posterior part of the jugular foramen

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior bulb of the internal jugular vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mastoid air cells and mastoid antrum laterally (thin plate of bone between); cerebellum medially; facial canal in front

pearl: Mastoiditis or chronic otitis media can erode into the sinus and cause septic sigmoid (lateral) sinus thrombosis: spiking fevers, headache and edema over the mastoid from thrombosis of the mastoid emissary vein (Griesinger sign). The sinus is at risk in mastoidectomy.

name: Parietal emissary vein
function: Valveless vein passing through the parietal foramen to connect the veins of the scalp with the superior sagittal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Scalp veins near the vertex (tributaries of the superficial temporal and occipital veins)

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the parietal foramen beside the sagittal suture, just in front of lambda

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior sagittal sinus (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Loose areolar tissue layer of the scalp, parietal bone, sagittal suture

pearl: Scalp infection in the loose areolar (danger) layer can spread through it to the superior sagittal sinus, causing sinus thrombosis or meningitis.

name: Mastoid emissary vein
function: Valveless vein passing through the mastoid foramen to connect the sigmoid sinus with the veins behind the ear.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Sigmoid sinus

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the mastoid foramen behind the mastoid process, accompanied by a meningeal branch of the occipital artery

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Posterior auricular vein or occipital vein (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Mastoid process, occipitomastoid suture, occipital artery

pearl: Edema and tenderness over the mastoid from thrombosis of this vein (Griesinger sign) points to septic sigmoid sinus thrombosis complicating mastoiditis; it bleeds briskly in retrosigmoid craniotomy.

name: Occipital emissary vein
function: Inconstant valveless vein through the occipital bone near the external occipital protuberance, connecting the confluence of sinuses with the occipital vein.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Confluence of sinuses; also receives the occipital diploic vein

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through a small foramen in the squamous part of the occipital bone at the external occipital protuberance

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Occipital vein (flow may run in either direction)

details.label: Relations
details.value: External occipital protuberance, occipital artery, greater occipital nerve

name: Condylar emissary vein
function: Inconstant valveless vein passing through the condylar canal to connect the sigmoid sinus with the suboccipital and vertebral venous plexuses.
