details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Lower end of the sigmoid sinus (or superior bulb of the internal jugular vein)

details.label: Course
details.value: Passes through the condylar canal, which opens in the condylar fossa behind the occipital condyle

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Suboccipital venous plexus, venous plexus around the vertebral artery and deep cervical vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Occipital condyle, atlantooccipital joint, vertebral artery; a meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery shares the canal

pearl: Links the dural sinuses to the valveless vertebral venous plexus, an alternative outflow of the brain in the upright position and a route for spread of infection or tumor.

name: Petrosal vein
function: Short, large vein in the cerebellopontine angle that collects the veins of the pons and the anterior cerebellum and empties into the superior petrosal sinus.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Transverse and lateral pontine veins, anterior pontomesencephalic vein, vein of the lateral recess of the 4th ventricle and cerebellar hemispheric veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs forward and laterally in the cerebellopontine angle cistern to the petrous ridge

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Superior petrosal sinus

details.label: Relations
details.value: Trigeminal nerve root just medial and below; facial and vestibulocochlear nerves behind; tentorium cerebelli above

pearl: Encountered next to the trigeminal root in microvascular decompression for trigeminal neuralgia and in cerebellopontine angle surgery; sacrificing it can cause venous infarction of the cerebellum or brainstem.

name: Inferior cerebral veins
function: Superficial veins draining the inferior surface of the hemisphere and the lower lateral cortex into the dural sinuses at the base of the skull.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the orbital surface of the frontal lobe and the inferior surfaces of the temporal and occipital lobes; lie beneath the arachnoid

details.label: Course
details.value: Run across the inferior surface of the hemisphere toward the nearest basal sinus

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Transverse, superior petrosal, cavernous and sphenoparietal sinuses; some join the basal vein (of Rosenthal) or the superficial middle cerebral vein

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli and floor of the anterior and middle cranial fossae

name: Deep middle cerebral vein
function: Drains the insula and the deep part of the lateral sulcus and is one of the roots of the basal vein (of Rosenthal).

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Insular veins in the floor of the lateral (sylvian) sulcus

details.label: Course
details.value: Runs medially in the depth of the lateral sulcus with the middle cerebral artery to the anterior perforated substance

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Joins the anterior cerebral vein and inferior thalamostriate veins to form the basal vein (of Rosenthal)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Insula, middle cerebral artery, optic tract and uncus

name: Veins of posterior cranial fossa (cerebellar and brain stem veins)
function: Veins of the cerebellum and brain stem, which leave the posterior fossa in three directions: upward to the great cerebral vein, forward to the petrosal vein and superior petrosal sinus, and backward to the straight and transverse sinuses.

details.label: Formed by / tributaries
details.value: Cortical veins of the cerebellar vermis and hemispheres and the surface veins of the midbrain, pons and medulla, continuous below with the anterior and posterior spinal veins

details.label: Course
details.value: Lie on the surfaces of the cerebellum and brain stem in the subarachnoid cisterns; they do not follow the arteries

details.label: Drains into
details.value: Great cerebral vein (of Galen) and basal vein; petrosal vein to the superior petrosal sinus; straight sinus, transverse sinuses and confluence of sinuses

details.label: Relations
details.value: Tentorium cerebelli above, falx cerebelli and occipital sinus behind, cranial nerves V to XII in the cisterns

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior group (to the great cerebral vein and basal vein): precentral cerebellar vein, superior vermian vein with preculminate and intraculminate veins, superior cerebellar vein, posterior and lateral mesencephalic veins; anterior group (to the petrosal vein and superior petrosal sinus): anterior pontomesencephalic vein, transverse and lateral pontine veins, anteromedian medullary vein, vein of the lateral recess of the 4th ventricle; posterior group (to the straight and transverse sinuses): inferior vermian vein, inferior cerebellar hemispheric veins, superior and inferior retrotonsillar veins
